# flowpanel

> The admin panel you don't have to build.
> Config-first admin panel framework for Next.js 16.

```bash
pnpm dlx @flowpanel/cli init
pnpm flowpanel migrate
pnpm flowpanel dev
```

Docs: https://flowpanel.tech/docs · Source: https://github.com/getflowpanel/flowpanel

Generated from the reference documentation. Property tables come from the
packages' own TypeScript declarations. Code blocks are excerpts from that
documentation: blocks the docs mark `twoslash` are type-checked in CI,
`excerpt` blocks are illustrative and may omit surrounding code.

## defineAdmin

The config entry point and every option it accepts.

Docs: https://flowpanel.tech/docs/reference/define-config

Documented types: defineAdmin, AdminConfig, AuthConfig, ThemeConfig, ShellConfig, AuditConfig, SecurityConfig, AuditEvent, LabelsConfig, CommandPaletteConfig, CommandGroup, CommandItem, ResolvedAdminConfig

`defineAdmin` is the only required call in your config. It takes one options
object, validates uniqueness (resource names, dashboard paths, queue keys),
wires the default bulk-delete action when applicable, and returns a
`ResolvedAdminConfig` that the Next.js bridge consumes.

`defineAdmin` is pure: it performs no I/O and does not mutate module-level
state. Importing a config from a page, script, or test has no external effect.

Every property table below is generated at build time from the package's own
TypeScript **source** — the same declarations the compiler reads — so a table
cannot drift from the type it documents.

### AdminConfig

`adapter` and `auth` are required. Everything else is optional, with sensible
defaults: no resources rendered, sidebar shell, English labels, no audit sink,
no realtime, no throttling.

`AdminConfig`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id?` | `string` | Stable id surfaced in the wire client metadata (`client.id`, default `"local"`) to tell multi-admin deployments apart. |
| `adapter` | `Adapter` | Database binding — `drizzleAdapter`, `prismaAdapter`, or your own. |
| `auth` | `AuthConfig` | How the admin reads sessions and roles. |
| `scope?` | `(ctx: ScopeContext) => Promise<Scope> \| Scope` | Tenant scope resolved per request, then applied to every query. |
| `theme?` | `ThemeConfig` | Branding, color scheme, design tokens and component overrides. |
| `shell?` | `ShellConfig \| ShellMode` | Chrome around the content area — sidebar, tabs, or none. |
| `labels?` | `LabelsConfig` | Override built-in UI strings. |
| `formatting?` | `FormattingConfig` | Locale, timezone and currency for numbers, money and timestamps. |
| `resources?` | `Resources` | Tables the admin manages. |
| `dashboards?` | `DashboardConfig[]` | Widget dashboards. |
| `pages?` | `PageConfig[]` | Custom pages rendered inside the shell. |
| `queues?` | `QueueConfig[]` | BullMQ queues surfaced in the admin. |
| `commandPalette?` | `CommandPaletteConfig` | What ⌘K offers. |
| `audit?` | `AuditConfig` | Audit trail for every mutation. |
| `realtime?` | `RealtimeConfig` | Cross-instance realtime transport. Redis in production. |
| `rateLimit?` | `RateLimitConfig` | Throttle requests per user or per IP. |
| `security?` | `SecurityConfig` | Browser request protections. Same-origin mutation checks are enabled by default. |
| `readOnly?` | `boolean` | Put the whole admin in read-only mode. |
| `paths?` | `AdminPathsInput` | Mount points for the generated admin UI and HTTP API. |
| `basePath?` | `string` |  |
| `hooks?` | `{ onError?: (err: Error, ctx: ErrorContext) => void \| Promise<void>; }` | Cross-cutting callbacks. |

### AuthConfig

The only part of FlowPanel that knows about your auth provider. `session` and
`role` run on every request and every page render, so keep them cheap — cache
inside your own session helper if they hit the network.

`session` receives the request being served, so a provider that reads cookies,
headers or the host — a tenant resolver, an OAuth callback check — can use it
directly. A helper that ignores the argument still satisfies the type.

`AuthConfig`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `session` | `(req: Request) => Promise<Session \| null>` | Reads the current session. Called on every request and page render, and handed the request being served so a provider that inspects headers, cookies or the host — a tenant resolver, an OAuth callback check — does not have to forge one. |
| `role` | `(session: Session \| null) => string \| Promise<string>` | Maps a session to a role string, which every `requireRole` gate compares against. |
| `requireRole?` | `string \| string[] \| ((s: Session \| null) => boolean)` | Admin-wide gate. Blocks every route and page before anything else runs. |
| `signInUrl?` | `string` | Where to send an unauthenticated visitor. Without it they get an inline notice. |
| `forbiddenUrl?` | `string` | Where to send a signed-in visitor who lacks the role. |
| `userId?` | `(session: Session \| null) => string \| null` | Extracts the actor id for audit rows and per-user rate limiting. |
| `allowUnauthenticated?` | `boolean` | Declares that this admin is meant to be reachable without any role gate — a deployment already fronted by a VPN or an authenticating proxy. Silences the development-only "no access control" warning. Production refuses to start without `requireRole` unless this is `true` AND the admin is `readOnly`. |

`requireRole` is the admin-wide gate, and nothing else in FlowPanel demands a
session: a config with no `requireRole` here, none on any resource, and no
global `scope` serves every route and page to anonymous visitors. `defineAdmin`
prints a warning about that in development. A deployment that is open on
purpose — behind a VPN or an authenticating proxy — sets
`allowUnauthenticated: true` to say so and silence the warning. Production is
stricter: a config without `auth.requireRole` refuses to compile unless it sets
both `allowUnauthenticated: true` and `readOnly: true`.

Four presets build an `AuthConfig` for you, all from `@flowpanel/kit/auth`
(`devAuth` is also on the package root):

| Preset | Session source | Role read from |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `withClerk(opts?)` | Clerk's `auth()` helper, loaded lazily | `sessionClaims.publicMetadata.role` |
| `withNextAuth(opts)` | the `auth()` / `getServerSession` you pass | `session.user.role` |
| `withLucia(opts)` | the Lucia instance you pass | `user.role` |
| `devAuth(role?)` | a fixed `{ id: "dev" }` | the `role` argument, default `"admin"` |

`devAuth()` is for local development and examples only: it authenticates
nobody, sets no `requireRole`, and leaves the "no access control" warning
firing.

See [Auth with Clerk](/docs/guides/auth-with-clerk) for the worked setup.

### ThemeConfig

`ThemeConfig`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `brand?` | `{ name?: string; logo?: string; href?: string }` | Product name, logo and home link shown in the shell header. |
| `accent?` | `string` | Accent color as an HSL triplet, e.g. `"220 90% 50%"`. An `hsl(…)` wrapper is unwrapped. |
| `accentDark?` | `string` | Dark-mode accent override, same format as `accent`. Custom accents tuned for light surfaces usually fail WCAG contrast on dark ones — pass a re-lightened triplet here to keep both schemes accessible. |
| `mode?` | `"light" \| "dark" \| "auto"` | Initial color scheme. `"auto"` follows the operating system. |
| `cssVars?` | `Record<string, string>` | Override any `--fp-*` design token, e.g. `{ "--fp-radius": "0.25rem" }`. |
| `cssVarsDark?` | `Record<string, string>` | Dark-mode token overrides, scoped to FlowPanel's dark roots and portals. Choose foreground tokens for contrast against the actual dark background. |
| `components?` | `Partial<FlowpanelComponentSlots>` | Replace built-in components. See the theme-slots guide. |
| `user?` | `(s: Session \| null) => \| { name?: string; email?: string; avatar?: string; items?: Array<{ label: string; href?: string; variant?: "default" \| "destructive" }>; signOut?: string; } \| undefined` | What the account menu shows for the current session. Return `undefined` to render no menu at all — the usual choice when there is no session. |

`components` is typed as `Partial<FlowpanelComponentSlots>` — see
[Theme slots](/docs/customization/theme-slots) for the ten shipped slots and how
to register your own.

`accent` and `cssVars` are emitted only on `[data-flowpanel-root]` and
`[data-flowpanel-portal]`. Dialogs and drawers carry the portal marker, so they
receive the theme without changing the host application's tokens.
`accentDark` and `cssVarsDark` target the same namespaced roots when
`html[data-flowpanel-theme="dark"]` or a FlowPanel root's `data-theme="dark"`
is active. Set `accentDark` whenever a custom `accent` is tuned for light surfaces;
use `cssVarsDark` when custom foreground or border tokens need dark-surface values.
Choose foreground values for contrast against the actual tinted background.
Every `--fp-*` token is overridable:

```ts excerpt
theme: {
  brand: { name: "Acme", logo: "/logo.svg", href: "/" },
  accent: "262 83% 58%",
  accentDark: "262 90% 72%",
  cssVars: { "--fp-radius": "0.25rem" },
  cssVarsDark: { "--fp-text-1": "0 0% 98%" },
}
```

Colors are HSL triplets, not `hsl(...)` calls, because the tokens are consumed
as `hsl(var(--fp-accent))`. Writing the wrapper form anyway is fine — it is
unwrapped for you.

`user` populates the account menu at the foot of the sidebar (or the right end
of the tab strip). Return nothing from it and no menu renders:

```ts excerpt
theme: {
  user: (session) => ({
    name: session?.user?.name,
    email: session?.user?.email,
    avatar: session?.user?.image,
    items: [{ label: "Settings", href: "/settings" }],
    signOut: "/api/auth/signout",
  }),
}
```

### ShellConfig

Pass a bare string when you only need the mode: `shell: "tabs"` is shorthand for
`shell: { mode: "tabs" }`.

`ShellConfig`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `mode?` | `ShellMode` |  |
| `brand?` | `{ name?: string; logo?: string; href?: string } \| false` | Overrides `theme.brand`. `false` hides brand even in sidebar/tabs. |
| `skipLink?` | `boolean` | Disable when the host application layout already renders a skip-to-content link. |

`ShellMode` is `"sidebar" | "tabs" | "bare"`:

- `"sidebar"` — full app shell with left nav and brand. The default, for
  standalone admins where FlowPanel owns the whole route.
- `"tabs"` — horizontal tab strip above the content, for admins embedded under
  a host app's existing header.
- `"bare"` — no chrome at all; your `app/layout.tsx` supplies it. Globals
  (toasts, drawer host, command palette, realtime) still mount.

The shell includes a skip-to-content link by default. Set `skipLink: false`
only when the host application layout already renders one for the same content
target; this avoids duplicate keyboard stops without removing the affordance.

### AuditConfig

`AuditConfig`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled?` | `boolean` | Turn auditing on. Individual resources can opt out with `audit: false`. |
| `sink?` | `(event: AuditEvent) => Promise<void>` | Where events go — your table, your log pipeline, anywhere. |

### SecurityConfig

Same-origin mutation protection is enabled when `security` is omitted. Add
exact `trustedOrigins` only when another frontend must write to the admin API.
Requests without browser `Origin` / Fetch Metadata headers remain available to
server-to-server clients.

`SecurityConfig`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sameOrigin?` | `boolean` | Reject cross-origin write requests using Origin and Fetch Metadata headers. Enabled by default. Disable only when an upstream gateway enforces an equivalent policy. |
| `trustedOrigins?` | `string[]` | Additional exact origins allowed to submit writes, for example `https://ops.example.com`. |

#### AuditEvent

What your `sink` receives. FlowPanel never writes audit rows itself — where they
land is entirely yours.

`AuditEvent`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `actorId` | `string \| null` | Who acted, from `AuthConfig.userId`. Null when unresolvable. |
| `action` | `string` | What ran, e.g. `"orders.action.refund"` or `"orders.inline-update"`. |
| `resource?` | `string` | Resource name the action targeted. |
| `targetId?` | `string` | Id of the affected row. Bulk actions carry the first ten, comma-joined. |
| `diff?` | `{ before: unknown; after: unknown }` | Before/after values, for mutations that can compute them. |
| `ip?` | `string` |  |
| `userAgent?` | `string` |  |
| `at` | `Date` |  |

### RateLimitConfig

`RateLimitConfig` is `RateLimitOptions` plus `per` (`"user"` or `"ip"`,
defaulting to `"user"`) and `enabled`.

```ts excerpt
type RateLimitOptions =
  | { driver: "memory"; limit: number; windowMs: number }
  | { driver: "redis"; url: string; limit: number; windowMs: number; keyPrefix?: string };
```

The memory driver counts per process — use the Redis driver whenever you run
more than one instance. A caller over the limit gets `429` from every API route.

### RealtimeConfig

An alias of `PublisherOptions`. Without it, realtime falls back to an in-process
bus that only reaches the instance that published — fine locally, wrong in
production. See [Realtime in production](/docs/guides/realtime).

### LabelsConfig

Overrides for built-in chrome. Set `labels` once in `defineConfig`; list filters,
pagination and the command palette use the same provider as action buttons.
Nested groups merge with English defaults. Undefined values keep their defaults;
empty strings are intentional overrides. A component's explicit placeholder or
boolean label takes precedence over configuration.

`allOption` controls the unfiltered choice in select, multiselect and boolean
filters. `filters` controls toolbar/reset text, boolean choices and text search.
`pagination.page` and `pagination.pageSize` accept `{n}`; `bulkBar.selected`
accepts `{n}` for selection counts. Pagination registry overrides receive these
strings in their `labels` prop; `DefaultPagination` remains usable standalone.

`navigation`, `table`, `savedViews` and `dateRange` also cover the built-in menu,
table controls, saved-view dialog and calendar. `dateRange.locale` controls
calendar and table-count presentation, with a deterministic `en-US` fallback on
both server and client. It does not change stored dates, query boundaries or
your custom column formatters.

`form` covers the generated create and edit pages: `createTitle` and `editTitle`
accept `{label}` for the resource's singular label, and `selectPlaceholder`,
`noOptions`, `searching` and `loadFailed` name the states of a select or a
reference search. The submit button uses `actions.create` on a create form and
`actions.save` on an edit form, and both pages offer a cancel link labelled with
`actions.cancel` that returns to the record or its list without submitting.

For a Russian admin, import `RU_LABELS` from `@flowpanel/kit` and pass
`labels: RU_LABELS` to `defineConfig`. The preset is a complete object of plain
strings, safe across the server/client boundary. Customize a nested group by
spreading it, for example `labels: { ...RU_LABELS, actions: {
...RU_LABELS.actions, new: "Добавить" } }`. Browser-only consumers can import the
same preset from `@flowpanel/core/labels`.

Resource names, domain actions, custom renderers and validation messages supplied
by your application remain application-owned. The preset does not translate
arbitrary content or server errors.

`LabelsConfig`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `noResults?` | `string` | Empty list state — used when a resource list returns 0 rows. |
| `allOption?` | `string` | Empty filter / select dropdown — the "any/all" sentinel. |
| `navigation?` | `{ skipToContent?: string; admin?: string; open?: string; title?: string; accountMenu?: string; account?: string; signOut?: string; scrollHint?: string; dashboards?: string; resources?: string; pages?: string; queues?: string; theme?: string; toggleTheme?: string; }` |  |
| `table?` | `{ /** Templates use `{n}`. Separate one/many templates avoid English suffixes. */ result?: string; results?: string; actions?: string; rowActions?: string; rowsHint?: string; rowsReadOnlyHint?: string; selectRow?: string; selectAll?: string; deselectAll?: string; }` |  |
| `dateRange?` | `{ /** Locale for calendar presentation; identical during SSR and hydration. */ locale?: string; label?: string; fieldLabel?: string; any?: string; clear?: string; clearAction?: string; from?: string; until?: string; previousMonth?: string; nextMonth?: string; firstMonth?: string; secondMonth?: string; pickEnd?: string; noSelection?: string; today?: string; yesterday?: string; last7d?: string; last30d?: string; thisMonth?: string; lastMonth?: string; MTD?: string; QTD?: string; YTD?: string; }` |  |
| `savedViews?` | `{ save?: string; saveTrigger?: string; name?: string; current?: string; label?: string; yours?: string; saveCurrent?: string; saved?: string; deleted?: string; delete?: string; storageError?: string; }` |  |
| `pagination?` | `{ label?: string; previous?: string; next?: string; of?: string; rowsPerPage?: string; /** Accessible page button name. Use `{n}` for the page number. */ page?: string; /** Page-size option. Use `{n}` for the row count. */ pageSize?: string; }` | Pagination chrome. |
| `filters?` | `{ label?: string; clear?: string; yes?: string; no?: string; searchPlaceholder?: string; }` |  |
| `bulkBar?` | `{ /** Use `{n}` for the selection count. Default: `"{n} selected"`. */ selected?: string; clear?: string; }` | Bulk action bar. |
| `searchPlaceholder?` | `string` | Resource search input placeholder. Use `{label}` for the resource's label. |
| `actions?` | `{ edit?: string; save?: string; cancel?: string; delete?: string; restore?: string; new?: string; create?: string; export?: string; import?: string; }` | Generic action buttons. |
| `form?` | `{ /** Edit page heading. Use `{label}` for the resource's singular label. */ editTitle?: string; /** Create page heading. Use `{label}` for the resource's singular label. */ createTitle?: string; /** The empty choice in a select control. */ selectPlaceholder?: string; /** A reference search with nothing to offer. */ noOptions?: string; /** A reference search still in flight. */ searching?: string; /** A reference search that failed. */ loadFailed?: string; /** An empty value the write needs. Use `{label}` for the field's label. */ required?: string; /** A value that is not a number. Use `{label}`. */ invalidNumber?: string; /** A value that is neither true nor false. Use `{label}`. */ invalidBoolean?: string; /** A value that is not a date. Use `{label}`. */ invalidDate?: string; }` | Generated create and edit form chrome. |
| `drawer?` | `{ close?: string; viewDetails?: string; }` | Drawer chrome. |
| `detail?` | `{ /** A fields tab with nothing the reader is allowed to see. */ noFields?: string; /** A tab naming a resource that is not registered. Use `{resource}`. */ unknownResource?: string; }` | Full-page detail chrome. |
| `related?` | `{ /** Link from a related tab to the target resource's own list. */ openList?: string; }` | Related detail-tab chrome. |
| `notFound?` | `{ title?: string; description?: string; back?: string; }` | The admin's own not-found page, for a URL no resource or dashboard matches. |
| `formError?` | `string` | Form-level banner shown when a submit fails with no field errors of its own. |
| `confirm?` | `{ title?: string; ok?: string; cancel?: string; }` | Confirm dialog. |
| `widget?` | `{ /** Zero-row state shared by tables, cards and charts. */ empty?: string; /** Link from a card heading to the full list. */ seeAll?: string; /** Freshness stamp on a refreshing dashboard. Use `{ago}`. */ updated?: string; justNow?: string; /** Use `{n}` for the second count. */ secondsAgo?: string; /** Use `{n}` for the minute count. */ minutesAgo?: string; /** Shown where a chart would be when @flowpanel/charts is missing. */ chartsMissing?: string; }` | Dashboard and detail-tab widget chrome. |
| `errors?` | `{ /** Failed page read. Use `{resource}` and `{operation}`. */ queryTitle?: string; /** What to check after a failed page read. */ queryHint?: string; /** Correlation line tying the card to the server log. Use `{id}`. */ requestId?: string; /** Failed widget, shown in the widget's own frame. */ widgetTitle?: string; widgetHint?: string; /** Button that re-runs a failed widget. */ retry?: string; }` | FlowPanel's own failure surfaces, shown in place of the data that did not load. |
| `palette?` | `{ placeholder?: string; noResults?: string; title?: string; description?: string; loading?: string; }` | ⌘K palette. |

#### CommandItem

`CommandItem`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` |  |
| `icon?` | `IconName` | Serializable Lucide icon rendered beside the label. |
| `shortcut?` | `string` | Shortcut hint shown on the right, e.g. `"⌘J"`. Display only — bind it yourself. |

### ResolvedAdminConfig

What `defineAdmin` returns. The lookup maps are precomputed so request-time
routing is O(1).

`ResolvedAdminConfig`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `__resolved` | `true` |  |
| `resources` | `Resources` |  |
| `resourcesByName` | `Map<string, ResourceConfig>` |  |
| `dashboardsByPath` | `Map<string, DashboardConfig>` |  |
| `pagesByPath` | `Map<string, PageConfig>` |  |
| `queuesByKey` | `Map<string, QueueConfig>` |  |
| `basePath` | `string` | Normalized `basePath` — leading slash, no trailing slash. Defaults to `/admin`. |
| `paths` | `AdminPaths` | Normalized mount points with leading slashes and no trailing slash. |
| `warnings` | `readonly string[]` | Config problems that do not stop the admin from booting — a create form that cannot satisfy a required column, so far. `flowpanel doctor` prints them, and development prints each one once. |

`defineAdmin` throws if two resources share a name, two dashboards or pages
share a path, or two queues share a key.

It also throws when a config points at a resource name nothing resolves to —
`reference.resource` on a column or field, a drawer or detail tab's `resource`,
or a `table()` widget's `resource`. The names it checks against are the
*resolved* ones, so a Drizzle table declared as `pgTable("ai_usage", …)` is
`"ai_usage"` even when the exported variable is `aiUsage`. The error names the
config path and suggests the near match.

Bind the definition with `createFlowpanel(config)`, then mount its page and
handlers. The runtime comes from `@flowpanel/kit/next`:

```ts excerpt
// app/admin/[[...slug]]/page.tsx
import { createFlowpanel } from "@flowpanel/kit/next";
import config from "@/flowpanel.config";

const flowpanel = createFlowpanel(config);

export default flowpanel.page;
```

```ts excerpt
// app/api/flowpanel/[...route]/route.ts
import { createFlowpanel } from "@flowpanel/kit/next";
import config from "@/flowpanel.config";

const flowpanel = createFlowpanel(config);

export const { GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, OPTIONS } = flowpanel.handlers;
```

### Default bulk delete

When a resource has delete enabled (i.e. **not** `delete: { disabled: true }`)
and declares no `bulkActions`, `defineAdmin` injects a default `delete` bulk
action. Set `delete.confirm` to replace its confirmation description. Opt out
with `bulkActions: []` or `delete: { disabled: true }`.

`readOnly: true` short-circuits the whole rule: a read-only admin rewrites
every resource to `bulkActions: []` (and empties `actions` and the drawer's
actions, disables create/update/delete, drops `import`, and clears every
column's `editable`), so no default delete is injected for any resource.

### Reserved names

`defineAdmin` also throws when a resource name or a queue key is one of
`dashboards`, `drawer` or `queues`. Those are the first URL segments the
admin's own routing claims — `handlers()` matches `drawer` and `dashboards`
positionally, and the page router matches `queues` — so a resource named after
one has its requests captured by the wrong route. The error names the option
to change (`options.name` for a resource, `options.key` for a queue).

### Behavior beyond validation

`defineAdmin` does three things to your config on the way through, besides
checking it:

1. **Fills `columns`** from `adapter.introspect(ref)` for any resource that
   omitted them, in introspection order. If the adapter cannot introspect the
   ref, or reports zero columns, that throws.
2. **Injects the default bulk delete** (above).
3. **Normalizes `basePath`** and every dashboard / page `path` — a missing
   leading `/` is added, a trailing one stripped.

None of it is I/O: `introspect` is a synchronous
read of a table object or DMMF, not a database round trip.

#### `basePath` and a Next.js deployment `basePath`

`basePath` and `paths.api` are app-relative: they say where the admin sits inside
your app, not where the app sits under a domain. If `next.config` sets its own
`basePath`, leave both alone — Next serves and links everything under that prefix
already.

FlowPanel adds the deployment prefix for you to the requests the browser issues
by itself: the client fetches built from `paths.api`, the generated form actions
and the SSE endpoint. `Link`, router navigation and `revalidatePath` are prefixed
by Next and are left untouched. Only a fetch you write yourself against
`paths.api` needs the helper:

```ts excerpt
import { withDeploymentBasePath } from "@flowpanel/kit/react"; // or "@flowpanel/core/paths" on the server

await fetch(`${withDeploymentBasePath(config.paths.api)}/user/u1/actions/verify`, {
  method: "POST",
});
```

#### Formatting

`formatting` decides how the admin renders values, on the server and in the
browser alike:

```ts excerpt
formatting: { locale: "ru-RU", timeZone: "Europe/Moscow", currency: "RUB" },
```

`locale` governs the `number` and `money` column formats and the date shape;
`currency` is the default for a `money` column that names none, and a column's own
`currency` still wins. `timeZone` is what the server and the first paint use — after
hydration a timestamp shows in the reader's own zone, which is what a
`LocalTime` has always done.

With no `locale`, dates keep the sortable `YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm` shape they had
before, and numbers keep `en-US` grouping.

#### Identifiers in URLs

Record identifiers are percent-encoded into the URL and decoded once when the page
route reads them back, so an id containing `/`, `%`, `?`, `#` or a space addresses
the record it names. Configured dashboard and page paths keep their separators —
`/reports/weekly` stays two segments.

A row whose projection did not include the key column is displayed but not treated
as addressable: no selection, no inline editing, no row activation. Keep the key
column in `columns`, or in `detail.tabs[].fields`, wherever the table has to act
on rows.

## resource()

Every option on a resource, its columns, fields and filters.

Docs: https://flowpanel.tech/docs/reference/resources

Documented types: resource, ResourceOptions, ColumnDef, formatColumnValue, formatNumber, FieldDef, FilterDef, DetailTab, DetailTabContext, ListResult, ResourceConfig

`ref` is whatever your adapter understands — a Drizzle table object, or a
Prisma model name. The row type comes from
[`InferRow<Ref>`](/docs/reference/registry#inferrow): a Drizzle table resolves
through `$inferSelect`, a string ref through your `FlowpanelResources`
augmentation, and anything else falls back to `Record<string, unknown>`. When
it resolves to a real row type, `columns`, `search`, `filters` and
`defaultSort` only accept real column names; when it falls back, they are
plain `string` and the check moves to
[`defineAdmin`'s introspect-time validation](/docs/build/resources#typos-and-column-validation).

```ts excerpt
import { resource } from "@flowpanel/kit";
import { orders } from "@/db/schema";

export const ordersResource = resource(orders, {
  label: "Order",
  plural: "Orders",
  icon: "shopping-cart",
  columns: ["id", "customerEmail", { field: "total", format: "money" }, "status"],
  search: ["customerEmail"],
  filters: ["status", { field: "createdAt", type: "daterange" }],
  defaultSort: { field: "createdAt", dir: "desc" },
  detail: { header: (row) => `Order · ${row.customerEmail}` },
});
```

### ResourceOptions

`ResourceOptions`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name?` | `string` | URL segment and registry key. Defaults to the adapter's table name. |
| `label?` | `string` | Singular label shown in headings and buttons. |
| `labelOne?` | `string` | Label for exactly one row, e.g. `"Customer"`. Used where a heading talks about a single record — the create page's title. Falls back to `label`, then to the resource name. |
| `plural?` | `string` | Plural label shown in the nav and list title. |
| `icon?` | `IconName` | Serializable Lucide icon rendered in navigation and the command palette. |
| `hidden?` | `boolean` | Keep the resource out of the navigation — its routes still work. |
| `expose?` | `(keyof Row & string)[]` | Additional fields shared by list and detail presentation. Declare render dependencies explicitly; callbacks never receive an undeclared DB row. |
| `columns?` | `(keyof Row \| ColumnDef<Row>)[]` | Columns of the list table, in order. A bare string is a field name. Omitted, `defineAdmin` fills it with every column the adapter introspects, in introspection order. |
| `search?` | `(keyof Row & string)[]` | Fields the search box queries. Without this, search is disabled. |
| `filters?` | `(keyof Row \| FilterDef<Row>)[]` | Filter controls above the list. A bare string always renders a text filter — declare a `FilterDef` for any other control. |
| `defaultSort?` | `{ field: keyof Row & string; dir: "asc" \| "desc" }` | Sort applied when the URL carries none. |
| `pageSize?` | `number` | Rows per page. Default: `20`. |
| `density?` | `"comfortable" \| "compact"` | Row height preset for the list table. Default: `"comfortable"`. |
| `rowClick?` | `"detail" \| "drawer" \| false` | What a row click — and Enter on the focused row — does. `"detail"` navigates to the row's own page, `"drawer"` opens the drawer and requires `drawer`, and `false` leaves rows inert. A row the projection cannot identify never acts. Default: ``"detail"` when `detail` is configured and `drawer` is not, `"drawer"` when only `drawer` is, otherwise `false``. |
| `rowKey?` | `keyof Row & string` | Property holding each row's unique id. Default: `"id"`. |
| `drawer?` | `DrawerConfig<Row>` | Side panel opened for a single row. |
| `detail?` | `{ /** * Extra fields used only by detail headers, hidden-tab predicates, related * filters, or custom detail renderers. They never widen list rows. */ expose?: (keyof Row & string)[]; /** Heading content (inside h1). Receives declared, readable detail fields; nullish output uses `<label> · <pk>`. */ title?: (row: Row) => ReactNode \| string \| null \| undefined; /** @deprecated Use `title`. Removed in 1.0. */ header?: (row: Row) => ReactNode; /** One line under the heading, for the fact that identifies the record. */ subtitle?: (row: Row) => string \| null \| undefined; /** Status pill beside the heading. */ badge?: (row: Row) => { label: string; tone?: Tone } \| null \| undefined; tabs?: DetailTab<Row>[]; fields?: (keyof Row \| FieldDef<Row>)[] \| "*"; }` | Full-page view at `/<basePath>/<resource>/<id>`. |
| `schema?` | `z.ZodTypeAny \| { create?: z.ZodTypeAny; update?: z.ZodTypeAny }` | Validation for writes. Overrides the schema inferred from the adapter. |
| `create?` | `{ disabled?: boolean; fields?: FieldDef<Row>[]; defaultValues?: Partial<Row> }` | Create form. `disabled` removes the route, not just the button. |
| `update?` | `{ disabled?: boolean; fields?: FieldDef<Row>[]; /** * Additional readable values available to edit-form hidden/readOnly * predicates. This never creates a control, default value, or write * permission. */ expose?: (keyof Row & string)[]; }` | Edit form. `disabled` removes the route, not just the button. |
| `delete?` | `{ disabled?: boolean; softDelete?: keyof Row & string; confirm?: string }` | Delete behaviour. Set `softDelete` to a timestamp column to keep rows recoverable. |
| `actions?` | `RowAction<Row, any, any>[]` | Per-row actions, rendered inline or in the row's menu. |
| `bulkActions?` | `BulkAction<Row, any, any>[]` | Actions applied to a selection of rows. |
| `scope?` | `"bypass" \| ((scope: Scope, query: unknown) => unknown)` | How the admin-wide `scope` narrows this resource. `"bypass"` opts out explicitly. |
| `access?` | `ResourceAccess<Row>` | Canonical operation-level authorization. |
| `fieldAccess?` | `FieldAccessMap<Row>` | Canonical read/write policy for declared fields. |
| `requireRole?` | `string \| string[] \| ((session: Session \| null) => boolean)` |  |
| `export?` | `{ formats?: ("csv" \| "json")[]; fields?: (keyof Row & string)[] } \| false` | Export button. `false` removes it. Defaults to CSV and JSON of the visible columns. |
| `import?` | `{ formats?: ("csv" \| "json")[]; fields?: (keyof Row & string)[] } \| false` | Import button. Off unless set; rows are created through the normal write path. |
| `audit?` | `boolean` | Opt this resource out of the admin-wide audit sink. |
| `realtime?` | `boolean \| string` | Refresh the list when the channel fires. `true` uses `resource.<name>`. |
| `views?` | `Array<{ name: string; description?: string; filters?: Record<string, unknown>; sort?: { field: keyof Row & string; dir: "asc" \| "desc" }; search?: string; }>` | Filter / sort presets offered as a dropdown above the list. |
| `empty?` | `{ /** Serializable Lucide icon rendered above the empty-state title. */ icon?: IconName; title?: string; description?: string; action?: { label: string; href: string }; }` | What the list shows when there are no rows at all. |

#### Detail headings and editing

Three callbacks fill the detail page's header, and each one receives the same
authorized row projection as detail tabs: declared readable fields plus permitted
`detail.expose` fields, never undeclared adapter fields and never fields denied by
`fieldAccess`.

- `detail.title(row)` is the content of the `h1`. Return text or inline React
  elements, not another heading or a complete page header.
- `detail.subtitle(row)` is the line under it, rendered through the header's
  `description` slot. Return a string.
- `detail.badge(row)` is a status pill beside the title: `{ label, tone }`, with
  `tone` from the shared `Tone` vocabulary.

```ts excerpt
detail: {
  title: (row) => row.email,
  subtitle: (row) => `Customer since ${row.createdAt}`,
  badge: (row) => (row.churned ? { label: "Churned", tone: "warn" } : null),
}
```

Return `null` or `undefined` from any of them and that slot is simply absent; a
nullish `title` falls back to the resource's singular label and the readable row
identifier. `detail.header` still works and still wins nothing: `title` takes
precedence when both are declared, and `header` is deprecated for removal in 1.0.

The generated edit action sits beside the heading; it is omitted when
`update.disabled` is true or the resource's update access policy denies the
request, including asynchronous policies. Set `labels.actions.edit` to translate
its text. The edit route enforces its own authorization as well. At narrow widths
the actions wrap below the title rather than squeezing it.

Custom `PageHeader` slots should use the exported `PageHeaderProps` type: `title`
accepts React content as well as strings, and `badge` takes the same
`{ label, tone }` object.

Without `detail.tabs`, the page renders one key/value block. `detail.fields`
chooses and orders the fields in it; omitted, every readable declared field shows.

#### Opening a row

`rowClick` decides what a click on a row — and Enter on the focused row — does.

| Value | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `"detail"` | Navigates to the row's own page under the admin's `basePath`. |
| `"drawer"` | Opens the [drawer](/docs/reference/drawer). Requires a `drawer` config; `defineAdmin` refuses the combination without one. |
| `false` | Rows render, but a click does nothing. |

Omitted, it follows the resource: `"detail"` when `detail` is configured and
`drawer` is not, `"drawer"` when only a drawer is, and `false` when neither is.
An explicit value always wins, so `rowClick: "detail"` on a resource that also
has a drawer sends the click to the page and leaves the drawer to its own
affordances.

A row the projection could not identify never navigates — the row identity rule
applies to the keyboard exactly as it does to the pointer, and the table's
"Enter opens" hint (`labels.table.rowsHint`) is announced only when some row on
the page can be opened. The mobile card list follows the same rule.

Navigation is a router push on the row, not a link: cmd-click, middle-click and
"open in new tab" do not open a second tab from a row. Reach the same page as a
real link through the detail page's own URL, or add a column whose `render`
returns an anchor.

#### Icons

`ResourceOptions.icon`, dashboard/page/queue icons, action icons and
`CommandItem.icon` all use the same serializable `IconName` union. FlowPanel
turns the name into a decorative Lucide SVG in the sidebar, tab strip and ⌘K
palette, so the config remains safe to pass through a React Server Component
boundary. Unknown names are rejected by TypeScript instead of disappearing at
runtime. Built-in names include `users`, `settings`, `layout-dashboard`,
`database`, `shopping-cart`, `archive`, `refresh`, `play`, `ban` and
`trash-2`; editor autocomplete shows the complete `IconName` set.

For custom pages and slots, render the same registry directly:

```tsx excerpt
import { FlowpanelIcon } from "@flowpanel/kit/react";

<FlowpanelIcon name="workflow" className="size-4" />;
```

### ColumnDef

An entry in `columns`. A bare string is shorthand for `{ field: "name" }`.

`ColumnDef`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `field?` | `keyof Row & string` | Row property this column reads. Omit only when `render` supplies the cell. |
| `label?` | `string` | Header text. Defaults to a humanized `field`. |
| `render?` | `(row: Row, ctx: RequestContext) => ReactNode` | Custom cell renderer. Runs on the server; receives the request context. |
| `sortable?` | `boolean` | Allow clicking the header to sort by this column. |
| `width?` | `number \| string` | Fixed column width, in px when a number. |
| `align?` | `"left" \| "center" \| "right"` | Horizontal cell alignment. Defaults to `"left"`. |
| `className?` | `string` | Extra classes on every cell in this column. |
| `hidden?` | `boolean` | Keep the column out of the table (still available to export and drawer). |
| `format?` | `ColumnFormat` | Declarative cell formatting — use instead of `render` where it fits. |
| `reference?` | `ReferenceSpec` | Resolve a foreign key to a label from another resource. |
| `editable?` | `boolean` | Allow editing this cell inline from the list. |

`field` is optional so a column can render a value no row property holds — a
join, something computed. Such a column must set both `render` and `label`,
never sorts or filters, and is skipped by export; see
[Joined or computed values](/docs/customization/column-renderers#joined-or-computed-values).

#### ColumnFormat

Declarative cell rendering — reach for this before writing a `render` function.

```ts excerpt
type ColumnFormat =
  | "badge"
  | "money"
  | "number"
  | { kind: "badge"; tones?: Record<string, Tone> }
  | { kind: "money"; currency?: string; scale?: number };
```

`Tone` is `"default" | "accent" | "ok" | "warn" | "err" | "info" | "muted"`.
The object form of `badge` maps each cell value to a tone:

```ts excerpt
{ field: "status", format: { kind: "badge", tones: { paid: "ok", failed: "err" } } }
```

#### Formatting values yourself

Two formatters back every cell, card and export, and both take the admin's
resolved `formatting`, so locale, currency and time zone come from one place.

`formatColumnValue` renders the string variants of `ColumnFormat`; `formatNumber`
renders a widget's `NumericFormat` (`number`, `currency`, `percent`, `bytes`,
`duration`). Both live in `@flowpanel/core`, so a server component may call them —
`@flowpanel/react` only re-exports `formatNumber` for client code.

### FieldDef

An entry in `create.fields`, `update.fields`, a `DetailTab`, or an action's
`form`. Every rule here is enforced on the server, not just in the UI.

`FieldDef`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `keyof Row & string` | Row property this field writes. |
| `label?` | `string` | Field label. Defaults to a humanized `name`. |
| `help?` | `string` | Hint rendered under the control. |
| `placeholder?` | `string` | Placeholder text for empty inputs. |
| `type?` | `FieldType` | Which control to render. Omitted, a declared field renders as `"text"` — or `"reference"` when `reference` is set. The adapter's column type is consulted only by the fully generated form a resource gets when it declares no `create.fields` / `update.fields` at all, and only maps number, boolean, date and json; every other column type renders as text there too. |
| `options?` | `\| ReadonlyArray<string> \| SelectOption[] \| ((ctx: QueryContext) => Promise<SelectOption[]>)` | Choices for `select` / `multiselect` / `radio`. A function resolves per request. |
| `reference?` | `ReferenceSpec` | Turn the field into a searchable picker over another resource. |
| `required?` | `boolean` | Mark the field required in the form. Server-side validation still comes from `schema`. |
| `readOnly?` | `boolean \| ((values: Partial<Row>) => boolean)` | Render non-editable. Enforced server-side, not just in the UI. |
| `hidden?` | `boolean \| ((values: Partial<Row>) => boolean)` | Leave the field out of the form entirely. |
| `requireRole?` | `string \| string[] \| ((session: Session \| null) => boolean)` | Restrict who may see and write this field. Enforced on every write route. |
| `validate?` | `\| z.ZodTypeAny \| ((value: unknown, values: Partial<Row>) => string \| null \| Promise<string \| null>)` | Per-field validation, run server-side after the resource schema. |
| `defaultValue?` | `unknown \| ((ctx: QueryContext) => Promise<unknown>)` | Value used when creating, for keys the operator left empty. |
| `span?` | `1 \| 2 \| 3 \| 4 \| 6 \| 12` | Width in a 12-column form grid. Defaults to full width. |
| `group?` | `string` | Fieldset heading this field is grouped under. |

#### FieldType

```ts excerpt
type FieldType =
  | "text" | "textarea" | "number" | "email" | "password" | "url"
  | "date" | "datetime" | "time"
  | "boolean" | "switch" | "checkbox"
  | "select" | "multiselect" | "radio"
  | "json" | "markdown" | "tags" | "reference" | "hidden" | "color";
```

Omit it on a declared field and the control is `"text"` — or `"reference"`
when the field sets `reference`. The adapter's `ColumnMeta.type` is consulted
only by the fully generated form a resource gets when it declares **no**
`create.fields` / `update.fields` at all, and even there it only maps
`number`, `boolean`, `date` and `json`; every other column type renders as
text. So `enum`, `array` and `reference` columns need an explicit `type` (plus
`options` / `reference`) to get a richer control.

### FilterDef

An entry in `filters`. A bare string is **always** a `text` filter — there is
no inference from the column's type, so declare a `FilterDef` with an explicit
`type` for a select, a date range, or anything else.

`FilterDef`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `field` | `keyof Row & string` | Row property this filter narrows. |
| `label?` | `string` | Control label. Defaults to a humanized `field`. |
| `type` | `FilterType` | Which control to render, and how the value is encoded in the URL. |
| `options?` | `\| ReadonlyArray<string> \| SelectOption[] \| ((ctx: QueryContext) => Promise<SelectOption[]>)` | Choices for `select` / `multiselect`. A function is resolved per request. |
| `defaultValue?` | `unknown` | Applied until the operator picks a value of their own. |
| `hidden?` | `boolean` | Apply the filter without showing a control for it. |

#### FilterType

```ts excerpt
type FilterType =
  | "text" | "select" | "multiselect"
  | "daterange" | "numeric-range" | "boolean" | "tag";
```

`daterange` and `numeric-range` reach your adapter as a `FilterRangeValue`;
`multiselect` as a `FilterInValue`. Both are documented under
[Contexts](/docs/reference/contexts#filter-values).

### DetailTab

A tab on the full-page detail view at `/<basePath>/<resource>/<id>`.

The tab in view is the `?tab=<key>` search parameter — a real query parameter the
server reads, not a URL fragment — so a tab is linkable, bookmarkable and survives
a reload. Only the selected tab runs on the server; the others render their label
and nothing else.

A tab declares exactly one kind of content, and they resolve in this order:
`render`, `widgets`, `resource`, then fields.

#### Fields and sections

`fields` renders a flat key/value view; `"*"` shows every readable field. Each
entry is a bare field name or a `FieldDef`, whose `label` overrides the column
header the list page uses. Column `format` and `render` from `columns` apply here
too, so a value reads the same on both pages.

`sections` groups those fields into titled blocks and wins over `fields` on the
same tab:

```ts excerpt
{
  key: "overview",
  label: "Overview",
  sections: [
    { label: "Identity", fields: ["email", "name"] },
    { label: "Billing", fields: [{ name: "mrr", label: "MRR" }, "plan"] },
  ],
}
```

Fields named by `fields` or by any `sections` entry are declared dependencies:
they are added to the tab's projection and loaded when that tab is the one in
view. A tab that ends up with nothing the reader may see shows
`labels.detail.noFields`.

#### Widgets

`widgets` puts dashboard widgets in a detail tab, in the dashboard's own grid —
see [widgets in detail tabs](/docs/build/dashboards#widgets-in-detail-tabs).
`columns` sets the grid width, defaulting to 2. Each widget's `ctx.row` is the
record being viewed, and each one renders inside its own error boundary, so a
query that fails costs you that card and not the page. Declaring `widgets: []` is
still a widgets tab — it renders empty rather than falling through to the other
modes, because an empty array is a typo, not a choice.

#### Related rows

A tab with a `resource` renders that resource's list columns and paginates under
its own URL key `relatedPage.<key>` — so two tabs page independently and Back,
Forward and reload restore the page the reader was on. Reference columns resolve
to the referenced row's label, exactly as they do on a list page and in a table
widget.

`hide` drops columns before anything is rendered, and the hidden fields are also
projected out of the rows sent to the browser; the parent foreign key is the usual
candidate, since every row in the tab shares it. The tab's own row key is always
kept, since the table needs it for row identity. A hidden column cannot be sorted
from the URL either.

An "Open list →" link appears only when it would tell the truth: every filter
value has to be a scalar (`string`, `number`, `boolean` or `bigint`) and every
filter field has to be one the target resource declares, since the list page
accepts `?f_<field>=<value>` on no other terms. A tab filtered on a range, an `in`
set, or an undeclared field keeps its rows and drops the link. `sort` sets the tab's
default order, falling back to the target's `defaultSort` and then to its primary
key. Clicking a header re-sorts through the URL key `relatedSort.<key>`, written
as `<field>.<asc|desc>` and accepted only for a visible column the target
resource really has. Above the table, an "Open list →" link
(`labels.related.openList`) leads to the target's own list page with the
relationship already applied as `?f_<field>=<value>`, so the full paginated list
is one click away.

The tab's `filter` is a constraint, not a refinement: an undefined parent value or
a field the reader may not read yields no rows and no query.

#### Custom content

`render(row, ctx)` returns whatever you like. `row` is the projected row — the
declared and `detail.expose` fields, nothing else — and `ctx` is a
[`DetailTabContext`](#detailtabcontext): `db`, `session`, `dateRange`, `href`,
`labels` and the per-request `query` memo, the same pieces a widget query gets.

`DetailTab`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `key` | `string` | Stable identifier, stored in the URL's `?tab=` search parameter. |
| `label` | `string` | Tab label. |
| `hidden?` | `(row: Row) => boolean` | Hide the tab for rows that should not show it. |
| `fields?` | `(keyof Row \| FieldDef<Row>)[] \| "*"` | Field list to render as a key/value view. `"*"` shows every column. |
| `sections?` | `Array<{ label: string; fields: (keyof Row \| FieldDef<Row>)[] }>` | Grouped key/value fields, one block per entry. Wins over `fields`. |
| `resource?` | `ResourceName` | Render rows of a related resource instead of fields. |
| `filter?` | `(row: Row) => Record<string, unknown>` | Filter applied to `resource`, derived from the row being viewed. |
| `hide?` | `string[]` | Related-tab columns to omit, typically the parent foreign key. |
| `sort?` | `{ field: string; dir: "asc" \| "desc" }` | Related-tab default sort; falls back to the target's `defaultSort`, then its primary key. |
| `widgets?` | `WidgetConfig[]` | Dashboard widgets with `ctx.row` set to the record being viewed. |
| `columns?` | `1 \| 2 \| 3 \| 4 \| 6 \| 12` | Grid columns for `widgets`. Default: `2`. |
| `render?` | `(row: Row, ctx: DetailTabContext) => ReactNode` | Render arbitrary content instead of fields, widgets or a related resource. |

### DetailTabContext

What `DetailTab.render` receives as its second argument.

`DetailTabContext`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `db` | `DB` | Your database client, exactly as handed to the adapter. |
| `session` | `Session \| null` |  |
| `dateRange` | `ResolvedDateRange` | Range chosen in the dashboard's date picker, already resolved to dates. |
| `href` | `( resource: ResourceName, id?: string \| number, opts?: { filter?: Record<string, unknown>; tab?: string }, ) => string` | Mount-aware link builder; never hand-type `"/admin/…"` in a config. |
| `labels` | `ResolvedLabels` | The admin's resolved chrome strings, so a widget never hard-codes English. |
| `query` | `<T>(key: string, fn: () => Promise<T>) => Promise<T>` | Memoises `fn` for the current request so two widgets share one query. A failure is memoised too — the request does not retry under the same key. |
| `sql` | `<Row = Record<string, unknown>>( strings: TemplateStringsArray, ...values: unknown[] ) => Promise<Row[]>` | One read-only statement, as a tagged template. Every interpolated value is bound as a parameter, so `${input}` can never change the statement. `Date` binds as an ISO-8601 string and `bigint` as decimal text. Throws when the configured adapter implements no `sql` capability. Runs exactly the statement you write: no tenant scope, no access rule and no soft-delete filter are applied. Add those predicates yourself, or use `count` and resource reads, which do. |
| `count` | `(resource: ResourceName, where?: Record<string, unknown>) => Promise<number>` | How many rows of a registered resource match `where`, through the same role, access and tenant-scope checks as any other cross-resource read. A resource the current session may not read counts `0`. |

### SelectOption

```ts excerpt
type SelectOption = { label: string; value: string | number | boolean };
```

Wherever `options` is accepted, you may pass `string[]`, `SelectOption[]`, or a
function resolved per request.

### ListResult

What a `list` returns, from the adapter through to the pagination control.

`ListResult`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `rows` | `Row[]` |  |
| `total` | `number` | Total matching rows across every page — drives the pagination control. |
| `page` | `number` | 1-based index of the page in `rows`. |
| `pageSize` | `number` |  |

### ResourceConfig

What `resource()` returns. You pass it to `defineAdmin`; you rarely read it.

`ResourceConfig`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `__kind` | `"resource"` |  |
| `ref` | `Ref` |  |
| `options` | `ResourceOptions<Row> & Options` |  |

## Actions

Row, bulk, dashboard and drawer actions — every option and what they return.

Docs: https://flowpanel.tech/docs/reference/actions

Documented types: rowAction, RowAction, bulkAction, BulkAction, dashboardAction, DashboardAction, DrawerAction, DrawerFieldFormSpec, ActionResult, ActionContext

An action is a server-side function the operator triggers from the UI. FlowPanel
gives you four places to put one, all sharing the same result type and the same
guard pipeline: the admin-wide role gate, the resource gate, then the action's
own `requireRole` — before `run` is ever called.

Actions never become Server Actions. They are POST routes under
`/api/flowpanel/…`, mounted by `handlers(config)`.

### RowAction

Offered on a single row, inline or in the row menu.

```ts excerpt
import { resource, rowAction } from "@flowpanel/kit";
import { orders } from "@/db/schema";

type RefundInput = { reason: string };

const refundOrder = rowAction<typeof orders.$inferSelect, RefundInput>({
  key: "refund",
  label: "Refund",
  icon: "circle-dollar-sign",
  variant: "destructive",
  confirm: { title: "Refund this order?", confirmLabel: "Refund" },
  requireRole: "admin",
  disabled: (row) => (row.status === "refunded" ? "Already refunded" : false),
  form: [{ name: "reason", label: "Reason", type: "textarea", required: true }],
  run: async (row, input, ctx) => {
    await refund(ctx.db, row.id, input.reason);
    return { ok: true, message: `Refunded ${row.id}`, refresh: true };
  },
});

resource(orders, {
  columns: ["id", "status"],
  actions: [refundOrder],
});
```

The form describes an action-specific `ActionInput`, not columns on the row.
Use `rowAction<Row, Input>()` to get exact types for both handler arguments and
compile-time checks for every `form[].name`. The helper returns the same plain
object you could write inline; it has no runtime cost.

```ts twoslash
import { rowAction } from "@flowpanel/kit";

type User = { id: string; status: "active" | "suspended" };
type SuspendInput = { reason: string; notify: boolean };

export const suspendUser = rowAction<User, SuspendInput>({
  key: "suspend",
  label: "Suspend",
  icon: "ban",
  form: [
    { name: "reason", type: "textarea", required: true },
    { name: "notify", type: "checkbox" },
  ],
  run: async (user, input) => ({
    ok: true,
    message: `${user.id}: ${input.reason}`,
  }),
});
```

`RowAction`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `key` | `string` | Stable identifier, used in the action's URL. |
| `label` | `string` |  |
| `icon?` | `IconName` | Serializable Lucide icon rendered beside the label. |
| `variant?` | `ActionVariant` | Button styling. |
| `placement?` | `"inline" \| "menu"` | `"inline"` renders a button in the row; `"menu"` puts it in the row menu. |
| `confirm?` | `ActionConfirm` | Ask for confirmation before running. |
| `form?` | `FieldDef<Input>[]` | Inputs collected before `run`, passed to it as `input`. |
| `inputSchema?` | `z.ZodType<Input>` | Cross-field input validation for trusted action code. |
| `outputSchema?` | `z.ZodType<Output>` | Required before arbitrary `data` may cross the client boundary. |
| `hidden?` | `(row: Row, ctx: RequestContext) => boolean \| Promise<boolean>` | Hide the action for rows it does not apply to. Evaluated server-side per row. |
| `disabled?` | `(row: Row) => boolean \| string` | Disable with a reason. A string is shown to the operator. |
| `access?` | `AccessRule` | Restrict the action to a role. Enforced before `run`. |
| `when?` | `(context: FieldWriteContext<Row>) => boolean \| Promise<boolean>` | Server-enforced row condition, evaluated only after a scoped row load. |
| `unsafe?` | `readonly "db"[]` | Explicitly opt trusted code into raw database access. |
| `requireRole?` | `string \| string[]` |  |
| `run` | `(row: Row, input: Input, ctx: ActionContext<InferDB>) => Promise<ActionResult<Output>>` | Server-side handler. Runs only after every guard has passed. |

`hidden` runs server-side for every row on the page, and the row's action list
is filtered before it reaches the client — a hidden action is not merely
invisible, its route returns `404` for that row.

### BulkAction

Applied to the operator's selection. `run` receives the ids, capped at 1000 per
request — the cap is a **rejection, not a truncation**: over 1000 ids the route
answers `422 too many ids (max 1000)` and `run` never executes, so nothing is
half-applied. Page your own batches if you need more.

`BulkAction`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `key` | `string` | Stable identifier, used in the action's URL. |
| `label` | `string` |  |
| `icon?` | `IconName` | Serializable Lucide icon rendered beside the label. |
| `variant?` | `ActionVariant` | Button styling. |
| `confirm?` | `ActionConfirm` | Ask for confirmation before running. |
| `form?` | `FieldDef<Input>[]` | Inputs collected before `run`, passed to it as `input`. |
| `inputSchema?` | `z.ZodType<Input>` | Cross-field input validation for trusted action code. |
| `outputSchema?` | `z.ZodType<Output>` | Required before arbitrary `data` may cross the client boundary. |
| `access?` | `AccessRule` | Restrict the action to a role. Enforced before `run`. |
| `max?` | `number` | Maximum selected ids accepted by this action. Default: `1000`. |
| `unsafe?` | `readonly "db"[]` | Explicitly opt trusted code into raw database access. |
| `requireRole?` | `string \| string[]` |  |
| `run` | `(ids: string[], input: Input, ctx: ActionContext<InferDB>) => Promise<ActionResult<Output>>` | Server-side handler, given every selected id. Capped at 1000 ids per call. |

Use `bulkAction<Row, Input>(definition)` when the bulk form has a typed
payload. Its handler receives `string[]` ids followed by that input.

When a resource has delete enabled and declares no `bulkActions`, `defineAdmin`
adds a default delete action. Opt out with `bulkActions: []`.

### DashboardAction

Rendered in a dashboard's page header. It gets no row — only the form input.

`DashboardAction`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `key` | `string` | Stable identifier, used in the action's URL. |
| `label` | `string` |  |
| `icon?` | `IconName` | Serializable Lucide icon rendered beside the label. |
| `variant?` | `ActionVariant` | Button styling. |
| `confirm?` | `ActionConfirm` | Ask for confirmation before running. |
| `form?` | `FieldDef<Input>[]` | Inputs collected before `run`, passed to it as `input`. |
| `inputSchema?` | `z.ZodType<Input>` | Cross-field input validation for trusted action code. |
| `outputSchema?` | `z.ZodType<Output>` | Required before arbitrary `data` may cross the client boundary. |
| `access?` | `AccessRule` | Restrict the action to a role. Enforced before `run`. |
| `unsafe?` | `readonly "db"[]` | Explicitly opt trusted code into raw database access. |
| `requireRole?` | `string \| string[]` |  |
| `run` | `(input: Input, ctx: ActionContext<InferDB>) => Promise<ActionResult<Output>>` | Server-side handler. Runs only after every guard has passed. |

Use `dashboardAction<Input>(definition)` for the same typed form contract
without a row type.

Set `hideActionsBar: true` on the dashboard to suppress the bar these render in.

### DrawerAction

Rendered in the drawer footer for the open row. Its `form` uses the lighter
`DrawerFieldFormSpec` rather than `FieldDef`.

`DrawerAction`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `key` | `string` | Stable identifier, used in the action's URL. |
| `label` | `string` |  |
| `variant?` | `"default" \| "destructive"` | `"destructive"` styles the button as dangerous. |
| `confirm?` | `string` | Ask for confirmation with this message before running. |
| `form?` | `DrawerFieldFormSpec[]` | Inputs collected before `run`, passed to it as `formData`. |
| `palette?` | `boolean` | Also offer the action in the command palette. |
| `access?` | `AccessRule` | Roles allowed to see and execute this action. |
| `when?` | `(context: FieldWriteContext<Row>) => boolean \| Promise<boolean>` | Server-enforced row condition evaluated after the scoped row load. |
| `unsafe?` | `readonly "db"[]` | Explicitly opt trusted code into raw database access. |
| `requireRole?` | `string \| string[]` |  |
| `run` | `( row: Row, formData: Record<string, unknown>, ctx: ActionContext<InferDB>, ) => Promise<ActionResult>` | Server-side handler. Runs only after every guard has passed. |

#### DrawerFieldFormSpec

`DrawerFieldFormSpec`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | Key this input contributes to the action's `formData`. |
| `type?` | `"text" \| "textarea" \| "select" \| "switch" \| "number"` | Control to render. Defaults to `"text"`. |
| `options?` | `string[]` | Choices for `select`. |
| `required?` | `boolean` | Reject an empty value. Enforced server-side. |
| `validate?` | `\| z.ZodTypeAny \| ((value: unknown, values: Record<string, unknown>) => string \| null \| Promise<string \| null>)` | Per-input validation, run server-side before `run`. |

### ActionResult

What every `run` returns. The success shape drives what the operator sees next.

`ActionResult`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ok` | `true` |  |
| `message?` | `string` | Toast shown to the operator. |
| `refresh?` | `boolean \| string \| string[]` | Revalidate after the action. `true` refreshes the current resource; a string publishes that one channel. |
| `redirect?` | `string` | Send the operator to this path once the action succeeds. |
| `download?` | `{ filename: string; data: string \| Blob \| Uint8Array; mime?: string }` | Hand the operator a generated file. |
| `filename` | `string` |  |
| `data` | `string \| Blob \| Uint8Array` |  |
| `mime?` | `string` |  |
| `data?` | `never` |  |
| `data?` | `Data` |  |
| `ok` | `false` |  |
| `error` | `string` | Message shown to the operator. Safe to display — never include internals. |
| `fieldErrors?` | `Record<string, string>` | Per-field messages, keyed by `FieldDef.name`, for actions with a `form`. |

`ActionInput` is the default `Record<string, unknown>` payload used when no
more specific input type is supplied.

Returning `{ ok: false, error }` is the way to fail a run cleanly — the message
reaches the operator verbatim, so keep internals out of it. Throwing works too:
a `FlowpanelError` maps to its own status, anything else becomes a generic
`500` with the detail logged rather than sent.

### ActionContext

The last argument to every `run`.

`ActionContext`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `db` | `Db` |  |
| `unsafe?` | `{ db: Db }` | Explicit escape hatch for trusted action implementations. |
| `actorId` | `string \| null` | Caller identity — same derivation the audit trail uses (`auth.userId`, then `session.id`, then `session.user.id`). |
| `publish` | `(channel: string, payload?: unknown) => Promise<void>` | Push a realtime message to every connected admin. |

`ctx.db` is your own client — the adapter hands it through untouched, so you
write ordinary queries. `ctx.publish` pushes a realtime message to every
connected admin; widgets and lists that name the channel in `realtime` refresh.

### Validation

An action with a `form` is validated server-side before `run`:

1. `required` fields must be present.
2. Each field's `validate` runs — a Zod schema or a function returning a message.
3. Only then does `run` receive `input`.

A failure returns `422` with an `issues` array. The client renders them against
the matching inputs.

## Drawer

The row side panel — layout, tabs and actions.

Docs: https://flowpanel.tech/docs/reference/drawer

Documented types: DrawerConfig, DrawerTabFields, DrawerTabResource, DrawerTabWidgets, DrawerAction, DrawerPayload

A drawer is the fast path to one row: it opens over the list without losing the
operator's place, their filters or their scroll position. Declare it on a
resource and set `rowClick: "drawer"` to open it by clicking the row.

```ts excerpt
resource(orders, {
  columns: ["id", "customerEmail", "status"],
  rowClick: "drawer",
  drawer: {
    width: "xl",
    header: (row) => `Order ${row.id}`,
    tabs: [
      { key: "summary", label: "Summary", fields: "*" },
      { key: "items", label: "Items", resource: "orderItems", filter: (row) => ({ orderId: row.id }) },
    ],
    actions: [
      {
        key: "refund",
        label: "Refund",
        variant: "destructive",
        requireRole: "admin",
        confirm: "Refund this order?",
        form: [{ name: "reason", type: "textarea", required: true }],
        run: async (row, formData, ctx) => {
          await refund(ctx.db, row.id, formData.reason as string);
          return { ok: true, message: "Refunded", refresh: true };
        },
      },
    ],
  },
});
```

### DrawerConfig

`DrawerConfig`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `width?` | `DrawerWidth` | Panel width. Default: `"lg"`. |
| `header?` | `(row: Row) => string` | Panel title. Defaults to the row's key. |
| `fields?` | `DrawerFieldList<Row>` | Fields shown when no `tabs` are declared. `"*"` shows every column. |
| `tabs?` | `DrawerTab<Row>[]` | Tabs to render instead of a flat field list. |
| `actions?` | `DrawerAction<Row>[]` | Buttons rendered in the panel footer. |

`DrawerWidth` is `"sm" | "md" | "lg" | "xl" | "2xl" | "full"`, defaulting to
`"lg"`.

Without `tabs`, the panel renders `fields` as a flat key/value list. Field
labels come from the matching column's `label`, and any column with a `render`
function is rendered with it — so a status badge looks the same in the drawer as
in the table.

`fields` is `DrawerFieldList<Row>` — the same shape as `detail.fields`:
`(keyof Row | FieldDef<Row>)[] | "*"`. A key your row does not have is a compile
error, not an empty row in the panel.

### Tabs

`DrawerTab` is a union of three shapes, discriminated by which key you set.

#### DrawerTabFields

The row's own fields.

`DrawerTabFields`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `key` | `string` | Stable identifier for the tab. |
| `label` | `string` |  |
| `fields` | `DrawerFieldList<Row>` | Fields to show. `"*"` shows every declared column. |

#### DrawerTabResource

Rows of a related resource, filtered by the open row.

`DrawerTabResource`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `key` | `string` |  |
| `label` | `string` |  |
| `resource` | `ResourceName` | Related resource to list. Must be registered on the same admin. |
| `filter?` | `(row: Row) => Record<string, unknown>` | Filter applied to the related resource, derived from the open row. |

The related resource's own `requireRole` still applies. A tab the operator may
not read comes back empty rather than failing the whole panel.

A resource tab shows the **first 20 rows** and nothing more. There is no
pagination, no "load more", and no count of what was left out — the drawer
route reads one page of 20 and serializes it. For a relation that can exceed
that, link to the target resource's own list (filtered) instead of leaning on
the tab.

#### DrawerTabWidgets

Dashboard widgets, scoped to the open row.

`DrawerTabWidgets`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `key` | `string` |  |
| `label` | `string` |  |
| `widgets` | `Exclude<WidgetConfig, CustomWidget>[]` | `custom()` widgets are not renderable here — the drawer serializes over the wire. |

`custom()` widgets are rejected here at compile time. The drawer payload is
serialized over the wire, and a React component cannot cross it — use a widget
tab of metrics/charts/tables, or a `detail` tab, which renders on the server.

Each widget in the tab is flattened to a `SerializedWidget` before it crosses:
a discriminated union over `kind`, one variant per widget type.

```ts excerpt
type SerializedWidget =
  | { kind: "metric"; label: string; value: number | string; /* format, sublabel, tone, span, realtime */ }
  | { kind: "table"; rows: Record<string, unknown>[]; columns: { field: string; label?: string }[]; /* … */ }
  | { kind: "statGroup"; stats: { label: string; value: unknown; /* … */ }[]; /* … */ }
  | { kind: "chart"; subkind: "area" | "bar" | "line" | "pie"; label: string; dataPoints: number; /* … */ }
  | { kind: "unsupported"; label?: string; reason: string; span?: number };
```

The queries have already run by then — a metric carries its resolved `value`,
a chart carries only how many points it produced. A widget whose query throws
comes back as `{ kind: "unsupported", reason }` with a client-safe message, so
one failing widget does not take the panel down with it.

### Actions

Buttons in the panel footer. See [Actions](/docs/reference/actions#draweraction)
for `DrawerAction` and its form spec.

Drawer actions go through the same guard pipeline as every other write: the
admin-wide role gate, the resource gate, the action's own `requireRole`, then
input validation — all before `run`. An action the current operator cannot run
is omitted from the drawer payload as well as blocked server-side. Setting
`palette: true` also surfaces an authorized action in ⌘K.

`DrawerAction`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `key` | `string` | Stable identifier, used in the action's URL. |
| `label` | `string` |  |
| `variant?` | `"default" \| "destructive"` | `"destructive"` styles the button as dangerous. |
| `confirm?` | `string` | Ask for confirmation with this message before running. |
| `form?` | `DrawerFieldFormSpec[]` | Inputs collected before `run`, passed to it as `formData`. |
| `palette?` | `boolean` | Also offer the action in the command palette. |
| `access?` | `AccessRule` | Roles allowed to see and execute this action. |
| `when?` | `(context: FieldWriteContext<Row>) => boolean \| Promise<boolean>` | Server-enforced row condition evaluated after the scoped row load. |
| `unsafe?` | `readonly "db"[]` | Explicitly opt trusted code into raw database access. |
| `requireRole?` | `string \| string[]` |  |
| `run` | `( row: Row, formData: Record<string, unknown>, ctx: ActionContext<InferDB>, ) => Promise<ActionResult>` | Server-side handler. Runs only after every guard has passed. |

### The payload

What `GET /api/flowpanel/drawer/<resource>/<id>` answers with — worth knowing if
you render the drawer yourself.

`DrawerPayload`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `row` | `Record<string, unknown>` |  |
| `header` | `string` |  |
| `resourceLabel` | `string` | The resource's display label, so the drawer never shows the raw registry name. |
| `width` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg" \| "xl" \| "2xl" \| "full"` |  |
| `fields` | `SerializedFieldList` |  |
| `tabs` | `SerializedDrawerTab[] \| null` |  |
| `actions` | `SerializedDrawerAction[]` |  |
| `prerendered` | `Record<string, string>` | Field → HTML for fields whose column declares a `render`. |
| `labels` | `Record<string, string>` | Field → column label, so drawer rows read like their table headers. |
| `formats` | `Record<string, ColumnFormat>` | Field → column `format`. Plain data, rendered client-side exactly as the table does. |
| `detailHref` | `string \| null` | The record's own page, when the resource configures `detail`. |

### What crosses to the client

The drawer payload carries only the resource's **declared** surface — the
columns and fields you listed, never the raw adapter row. Columns with a
`render` function are pre-rendered to HTML on the server, so your renderer can
touch server-only data without shipping it.

## Widgets

Every widget builder and the options it accepts.

Docs: https://flowpanel.tech/docs/reference/widgets

Documented types: WidgetContext, metric, MetricOptions, MetricResult, MetricDelta, table, TableWidgetOptions, WidgetColumn, statGroup, StatGroupOptions, StatItem, stat, StatOptions, StatResult, kv, KvOptions, KvItem, bars, BarsOptions, BarRow, funnel, FunnelOptions, FunnelStep, list, ListOptions, ListRow, custom, CustomOptions, ChartOptionsBase, areaChart, AreaChartOptions, barChart, BarChartOptions, lineChart, LineChartOptions, pieChart, PieChartOptions, previousRange, fillDays, dashboard, page, DashboardConfig, SectionConfig, DateRangeConfig, ResolvedDateRange, PageConfig

Widgets are the contents of a dashboard section, and of a drawer's widget tab.
Each builder returns a `WidgetConfig`; every `query` runs on the server with a
`WidgetContext`.

```ts excerpt
import { dashboard, metric, statGroup, table } from "@flowpanel/kit";
import { areaChart } from "@flowpanel/kit/charts";

export const overview = dashboard({
  path: "/",
  label: "Overview",
  dateRange: { preset: "last30d" },
  sections: [
    {
      label: "Revenue",
      widgets: [
        metric("MRR", async ({ db, dateRange }) => mrr(db, dateRange), {
          format: "currency",
          span: 3,
          drilldown: "/admin/invoices",
        }),
        areaChart("Revenue over time", async ({ db }) => revenueSeries(db), {
          x: "day",
          y: ["subscriptions", "one-off"],
          stacked: true,
          span: 9,
        }),
      ],
    },
  ],
});
```

### WidgetContext

What every widget `query` receives.

`WidgetContext`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `db` | `DB` | Your database client, exactly as handed to the adapter. |
| `session` | `Session \| null` |  |
| `dateRange` | `ResolvedDateRange` | Range chosen in the dashboard's date picker, already resolved to dates. |
| `req` | `Request` |  |
| `row?` | `Record<string, unknown>` | Row of the record being viewed when the widget sits in a detail tab. |
| `href` | `( resource: ResourceName, id?: string \| number, opts?: { filter?: Record<string, unknown>; tab?: string }, ) => string` | Mount-aware link builder; never hand-type `"/admin/…"` in a config. |
| `query` | `<T>(key: string, fn: () => Promise<T>) => Promise<T>` | Memoises `fn` for the current request so two widgets share one query. A failure is memoised too — the request does not retry under the same key. |
| `labels` | `ResolvedLabels` | The admin's resolved chrome strings, so a widget never hard-codes English. |
| `sql` | `<Row = Record<string, unknown>>( strings: TemplateStringsArray, ...values: unknown[] ) => Promise<Row[]>` | One read-only statement, as a tagged template. Every interpolated value is bound as a parameter, so `${input}` can never change the statement. `Date` binds as an ISO-8601 string and `bigint` as decimal text. Throws when the configured adapter implements no `sql` capability. Runs exactly the statement you write: no tenant scope, no access rule and no soft-delete filter are applied. Add those predicates yourself, or use `count` and resource reads, which do. |
| `count` | `(resource: ResourceName, where?: Record<string, unknown>) => Promise<number>` | How many rows of a registered resource match `where`, through the same role, access and tenant-scope checks as any other cross-resource read. A resource the current session may not read counts `0`. |

`href` builds a link under the admin's own `basePath`, so a config never
hand-types `/admin/…`. `href("orders")` is the list, `href("orders", id)` one
record, and the third argument adds the list page's own query keys —
`{ filter: { status: "paid" } }` becomes `?f_status=paid` and `{ tab: "activity" }`
becomes `?tab=activity`.

`query(key, fn)` memoises for the request. Two widgets that need the same figure
pass the same key and the query runs once; the memo is per page render, so the
next request queries again. The memo holds the promise, so a failure is shared
too — the request does not retry under that key.

`labels` is the admin's resolved `LabelsConfig`, which is where a widget's own
wording should come from. `row` is present only when the widget sits in a detail
tab, and holds that record's projected fields.

```ts excerpt
metric("Paid orders", async (ctx) => ({
  value: await ctx.query("paid-orders", () => countPaid(ctx.db, ctx.dateRange)),
  href: ctx.href("orders", undefined, { filter: { status: "paid" } }),
}));
```

### Shared option types

`Span` is `1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 6 | 8 | 12` — the widget's width in the section's
12-column grid.

`NumericFormat` is `"number" | "currency" | "percent" | "bytes" | "duration"`.

`Tone` is `"default" | "accent" | "ok" | "warn" | "err" | "info" | "muted"`.

Every widget accepts `realtime`, a channel name or list. When one fires, that
widget re-runs its query — the rest of the dashboard stays put.

### metric

`MetricOptions`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `icon?` | `string` | Rendered as-is next to the label. Any string — an emoji, a ligature. No icon-name lookup exists. |
| `format?` | `NumericFormat` | How the number is rendered. |
| `sublabel?` | `string` | Small caption under the value. |
| `delta?` | `(ctx: WidgetContext) => Promise<MetricDelta \| null>` | Period-over-period change, queried alongside the value. |
| `sparkline?` | `(ctx: WidgetContext) => Promise<number[]>` | Trend line drawn inside the card. |
| `tone?` | `Tone` | Semantic color of the value. |
| `drilldown?` | `string` | Turns the whole card into a link to this path. |
| `span?` | `Span` | Width in the dashboard's 12-column grid. |
| `realtime?` | `string \| string[]` | Re-run the query when any of these channels fire. |

`icon` is handed to the metric card as a React child and rendered verbatim.
Metric icons are deliberately free-form: pass an emoji or a ligature your own
icon font resolves; a Lucide name renders as literal text. This differs from
resource, action and command icons, which use the serializable `IconName`
registry described under [resource icons](/docs/reference/resources#icons).

A `metric()` query may return a bare number or string, or a `MetricResult`
carrying the presentation the value itself implies. A result field wins over the
matching static option, which stays as the fallback.

#### MetricResult

`MetricResult`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `number \| string` |  |
| `tone?` | `Tone` |  |
| `sublabel?` | `string` |  |
| `delta?` | `MetricDelta` |  |
| `href?` | `string` | Turns the whole card into a link to this path. |

#### MetricDelta

`MetricDelta`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `number` | Fractional change — `0.12` renders as +12%. |
| `vs` | `string` | What the comparison is against, e.g. `"prior period"`. |
| `goodWhen?` | `"up" \| "down"` | Which direction is good news. `"down"` colours a fall green. Default: `"up"`. |

`goodWhen: "down"` colours a fall green — for churn, cost or latency a drop is
the good news.

### table

Point it at a registered `resource` to reuse that resource's columns, or supply
your own `query` and `columns`.

`R` is inferred from `query`, so `columns` is checked against the row that query
returns — a misspelled column is a compile error. A column entry is either a bare
key, which is `keyof R & string` once `R` is known and plain `string` while it is
not, or a `WidgetColumn` object naming and formatting a column the query produced
itself. A bare key on the `resource` path keeps that resource's declared header
and format; an object overrides them.

`TableWidgetOptions`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `label?` | `string` | Card heading. |
| `resource?` | `ResourceName` | Registered resource to pull rows and columns from. |
| `query?` | `(ctx: WidgetContext) => Promise<R[]>` | Supply rows yourself instead of reading a resource. |
